Accredited means you're on the books with the province, you DO teach the provincial curricula AND meet the provincial outcome standards.  You get provincial funding in this case, and the level (1 or 2) is determined by which set of instructional criteria you meet. The funding dollars are hard set, on a year by year basis, so the actual percentage varies a bit. Just look at the fine print on grocery store coupons; expires on this date, can/can’t be used with other coupons, $10 credit with a $100 purchase, have to buy 3 or more, etc.  

We have two coupons/credits; the Production Tax Credit (PTC) and the Net Operation Loss (NOL).
  
Here’s the fine print:
PTC: Can’t reduce the min production tax. Expire at the end of calendar year. Can be used with NOL.
NOL: Can be used to reduce the min production tax.  Does not expire. Can be used with PTC.

The order the coupons are used to reduce a company’s tax liability is the issue.  Companies have been applying the PTC first and then the NOL. The guidance states the NOL is applied first and then PTC.

For example, oil at $60bbl and a $2/bbl. NOL coupon; deducting the PTC coupon first and then the NOL coupon would result in $0 production tax. Switch the order.... Alaska receives $2/bbl production tax. Order matters.
